name: Parthian Fortresses of Nisa
description: Just outside Ashgabat in Turkmenistan, two great earthen mounds mark Old and New Nisa, an early Parthian city dating back more than 2,200 years. Much of it is still unexcavated, but digs have uncovered richly decorated buildings used for homes, government and worship. Reflecting Greek and Roman influences alongside local traditions, the site sat on busy trade routes between East and West.
